unclear_source_points: The automatic transcript renders PostgreSQL and Redis as similar-sounding words; the slides resolve both product names.

The course intentionally generalizes a very diverse NoSQL category. Sharding, transactions, query power, and partial-update semantics are product- and topology-specific, so the notes preserve the course model and label verified boundaries.

The statement that graph databases are not optimal for transactions is interpreted as a workload-fit warning, not a claim that graph databases lack ACID transactions; Neo4j documents ACID transaction support.

The exercise says to play around with three databases but does not prescribe versions, commands, data, outputs, authentication, or cleanup. The task labels its deterministic and safety requirements as Codex additions.
